title: Link text says shop.example.com but the link goes to www.example.com
evidence: site/about.html:15 shows the host shop.example.com as the link text. The href is www.example.com. The page's own canonical (about.html:6) is shop.example.com, so the text names the real shop and the target is a different host. The UK link on the same line (example.co.uk to www.example.co.uk) matches, so the mismatch is not a pattern of the whole line.
failing_case: A visitor reads 'Our shop lives at shop.example.com', clicks it, and lands on www.example.com, a host they were not told about. If that host is not the shop, they can enter card or login details on a site the page vouched for under another name.
remediation: Make the href and the visible text the same address (https://shop.example.com/), or change the text to the host the link really opens.

title: Dev live-reload script over http://localhost left in a shipped page, no integrity hash
evidence: Driven in Chromium with the CSP from _headers applied: 'Refused to load the script http://localhost:8080/reload.js' (script-src 'self'). The tag is still sent to every visitor. It is plain http, from another origin, with no integrity attribute.
failing_case: Every visitor's browser tries to load localhost:8080/reload.js and logs a CSP error. If the CSP is loosened later (for example to make the CDN script on line 8 work by adding a host or 'unsafe-inline'), whatever listens on a visitor's own port 8080 runs as script on the shop's origin.
remediation: Delete the tag from the committed page. Inject the reload script only in the dev server.

title: The map iframe is blocked by the page's own CSP and shows an empty box
evidence: No frame-src or child-src is set, so framing falls back to default-src 'self'. Driven in Chromium: 'Refused to frame https://www.example.org/ because it violates ... default-src self'. The iframe also has no sandbox attribute.
failing_case: A visitor opens About us and sees a blank frame where the map should be, with no explanation.
remediation: Add frame-src https://www.example.org to the CSP (and sandbox the frame), or replace the frame with a plain link to the map.

title: No viewport meta on login, about or checkout pages
evidence: Driven: document.querySelector('meta[name=viewport]') is null on all three pages. None has any stylesheet or width rule either. The same <head> pattern appears at about.html:4 and checkout.html:4.
failing_case: On a 390 px phone the browser lays the page out at about 980 px and scales it down, so the sign-in and card fields render tiny and the user must pinch-zoom to type a password or a card number.
remediation: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to each head, without user-scalable=no.

title: The page's own CSP blocks the third-party script it loads (login, about, checkout)
evidence: login.html:7 allows only 'self' scripts, yet login.html:8 loads cdn.example.org/widget.js. The same holds for about.html:8 (CSP adds only a nonce, and the tag has none) and checkout.html:7 (stats.example.org/t.js, covered by _headers:2). Driven in Chromium: 'Refused to load the script https://cdn.example.org/widget.js ... script-src self' on login; the same for lib.js on about and t.js on checkout. The request fails with 'csp'.
failing_case: Open any of the three pages. The widget, library and stats script never run. Whatever they provide (sign-in widget, site library, analytics) is silently missing, and the console shows the CSP error.
remediation: Decide per script. If it is needed, allow that exact host and its hash in script-src. If not, remove the tag. Keep the CSP in _headers as the single source and drop the per-page meta copies.

title: The integrity digest is placeholder text, not a hash, on all three third-party scripts
evidence: I base64-decoded the value: it is b'foobarbazfoobarbazfoobarbazfoobarbazfoobarbazqux', 48 bytes of ASCII filler, not a SHA-384 digest of any file. The identical value is on login.html:8, about.html:8 and checkout.html:7.
failing_case: Once the CSP lets the host through, the browser hashes the real file, finds it differs from 'foobarbaz...', and refuses to run it. The script stays dead, and the attribute gives a false impression that the script is pinned. On checkout.html a third-party stats script also sits on the page with the card field, so the digest matters most there.
remediation: Compute each digest from the exact file served (openssl dgst -sha384 -binary FILE | openssl base64 -A), pin the file version, and re-check it in CI. Better: do not load third-party scripts on the checkout page.

title: CSP nonce is a fixed string in a static page, and no script uses it
evidence: The nonce 'r4nd0m' is a literal in a static HTML file, so every visitor and every attacker gets the same value. None of the three <script> tags on lines 8, 9 and 10 carries a nonce= attribute. A nonce only protects when the server issues a fresh value on each response.
failing_case: Anyone who can inject markup into this page adds <script nonce="r4nd0m">...</script>. The CSP allows it, because the value is public and never changes. The nonce adds an injection bypass and protects nothing.
remediation: Drop the nonce and use hashes for any inline script, or generate a per-response nonce on the server and set it in the header and the tag together.

title: Checkout shows no order or total, collects only a card number, and the button just says Pay
evidence: The page has one field and one button. There is no amount, line items, expiry, security code or name field. The card input has no type or inputmode, so mobile keyboards are not numeric. There is no error or confirmation state markup.
failing_case: A user is asked to 'Pay' with no stated amount, so they cannot know what they are agreeing to. Most card processors also need an expiry and a code, so the submission cannot complete the purchase.

requirement.why: A checkout page is expected to show the amount and collect what a card payment needs; no spec is in the payload.

remediation: Show the order summary and total above the form, label the button with the amount ('Pay $42.00'), and add expiry and code fields with the right autocomplete tokens. Use inputmode="numeric" on the card number.

title: The Pay button can be submitted twice and nothing in the page guards a second charge
evidence: The form (checkout.html:12) is a plain POST to /pay. There is no disabled-on-submit, no idempotency key in a hidden field, no script on the page (the one script tag is blocked by the CSP).
failing_case: A user on a slow connection double-clicks or presses Enter twice on Pay. Two POSTs reach /pay. The browser aborts the first navigation, but the server may already have processed it, so the card can be charged twice unless the server dedupes. The server code is not in this payload, so that guard is unverified.
remediation: Put a one-time idempotency token in a hidden field and enforce it on the server. Also disable the button on the first submit.

title: Sign-in fields have no autocomplete tokens (WCAG 1.3.5, AA)
evidence: login.html:16 and :17 collect the user's own email and current password with no autocomplete attribute. Criterion 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA) requires the purpose of fields that collect user data to be programmatically determinable. The checkout card field on checkout.html:13 does set autocomplete="cc-number", so the omission is inconsistent.
failing_case: A user who relies on browser or assistive autofill to fill sign-in fields finds that the email and password are not filled reliably, and has to type both on every visit.
remediation: Add autocomplete="username" (or "email") to the email input and autocomplete="current-password" to the password input.

title: /js/site.js does not exist in the site, so every About load makes a 404
evidence: The project holds only site/about.html, checkout.html, login.html and _headers. No js/ directory exists. Driven against a server rooted at site/: GET /js/site.js returned 404.
failing_case: Every visit to About us requests /js/site.js and gets 404. Whatever the script was meant to do does not happen.
remediation: Add the file, or remove the tag if it is a leftover.

title: Link text 'index.html' names a file, but the link opens a docs site root
evidence: The href has no filename. The text reads like a download name, just after 'brochure.pdf' in the same sentence.
failing_case: A reader expects a file called index.html and instead lands on the docs home page.
remediation: Use link text that says where it goes, such as 'the documentation'.
